title: Static Fusiform Fork-Tail Fish
description: One original stylised whole fish exterior with a short rounded forward head, deep laterally compressed fusiform body, a distinct narrowed tail peduncle and vertically broad two-lobed tail with an actual concave trailing fork. A long raised dorsal fin, shorter lower anal fin and two swept lateral pectoral fins have finite thickness and grow through real removed shared-vertex ports in the new body: body and all fins are one connected closed mesh, not closed fin plates buried into a body. Two small closed dark lateral eyes are seated in the head. All axial sections, fin profiles, fork and eye placements are newly authored; this is not the museum skeleton filled with skin, an elongated ray disc, a tadpole with its tail trimmed, a snake straightened or a bat wing extracted. Only generic mesh orientation and the mature exporter/renderer are reused. Three editable closed meshes and four opaque constant matte PBR roles, no texture or transparency. Metres, native Z up, head/front -Y, full horizontal bounds-centred lowest-extent origin. One prop and zero scenes, species variants or life stages counted separately. Static artistic exterior only: no exact species, internal skeleton, gills, scales, biological anatomy, life-size, natural standing support, swimming, breathing, buoyancy, rig, animation, physical or ecological performance claim.
